title: Customer request orchestra: micro-themes & quick-win map
content:
Purpose:
Quick synthesis of customer asks from May–Jul 2029 intake (demos, support threads, AE notes). Goal: produce a compact set of micro-themes, 6 prioritized proposals (including 3 low-effort/high-impact), and engineering feasibility signals so PM/ENG can act fast.

Background/context:
- Intake sources: demo notes (AE), support tags (feature-request), weekly field sync, two on-site customer Gemba sessions (May 23, Jun 7), and a lightweight VOC survey (n=64).
- Primary product areas implicated: hosted API (routing / model fallbacks), console/rollouts (canary policies + visibility), optimize (batching/cost suggestions), private (VPC onboarding friction).

High-level micro-themes (framing language for GTM/PM):
1) Predictable fallbacks: customers want deterministic fallback behavior and visibility when model variants are used (explicit logs, fallbacks-as-config).
2) Batching visibility + overrides: teams need visibility into automatic batching decisions and a manual override knob per-route for latency-critical flows.
3) Eval-integrated rollouts: customers want rollouts tied to their eval prompt sets so canary pass/fail is measured on owned metrics (not just token error counts).
4) Cost transparency at token granularity: explain token vs compute cost for mixed-precision/quantized variants.
5) Private onboarding checklist gaps: networking/KMS steps unclear for infra teams; customers hit 3–5 back-and-forths during first week.
6) SDK ergonomics for streaming + function calls: edge cases where streaming chunks and tool-calls interleave cause client complexity.

Representative customer quotes (anonymized):
- "We need to know exactly when fallback happened and why — it breaks our audit for compliance."
- "Auto-batching is great but we had a latency explosion; wish we could opt out on a per-route basis."
- "Rollouts would be useful if they reported accuracy on our prompts — otherwise we're flying blind."

Quick-win (low engineering cost) proposals — prioritized for next 6 weeks:
A) Fallback visibility flag (opt-in): emit a small header in API responses when a fallback/variant was used and surface the model id + policy that triggered it.
   - Rationale: solves compliance + incident triage without changing routing logic.
   - Estimated effort: S (1–2 sprint days backend + console checkbox).
   - Suggested owner: product-hosted-api + eng-console.

B) Per-route batching override (config boolean + telemetry): allow routes to opt-out of auto-batching and surface a batching decision log in Console (last N minutes).
   - Rationale: customers with tail-latency needs can force single-request paths quickly.
   - Estimated effort: M (2–3 sprints: runtime flag + console toggle + telemetry plumbing).
   - Quick UX: toggle + explanation tooltip, fallback to default if misconfigured.

C) Private onboarding checklist doc + ephemeral runbook template: consolidate common KMS/VPC RBAC missteps, include sample Terraform snippets and port + IP checklist.
   - Rationale: non-engineering customers can run through onboarding with fewer support tickets.
   - Estimated effort: XS (content + one-page Console link).

Medium-effort proposals (quarter roadmap candidates):
D) Eval-tied rollout gating in Console: allow customers to bind a rollout to an eval set (their prompts), report pass/fail on customer metrics, and auto-rollback if threshold breached.
   - Impact: high for customers with strict quality SLAs.
   - Estimated effort: L (3+ sprints across backend, eval infra, console).

E) Token-cost breakdown per-response including quantization/precision: show estimated GPU-seconds and token billing split per model variant in usage exports.
   - Impact: medium-high for cost-conscious teams.
   - Estimated effort: M (2–4 sprints: billing + runtime instrumentation + export UI).

F) Streaming + function-call edge-case guide + SDK fixes: small SDK patches to normalize streaming+tool call boundaries and a guide for client-side reconcilers.
   - Impact: reduces client integration time.
   - Estimated effort: M (SDK sprint + docs).

Risk flags / unresolved tradeoffs (callouts):
- Fallback visibility increases surface area for support if fallback policies are misunderstood; need clear docs and OOB heuristics.
- Per-route batching override can be misused and increase cost; consider quota guardrails.
- Eval-integrated rollouts require secure handling of customer prompt sets (PII concerns) — coordinate with security/compliance.

Suggested prioritization rubric (simple, actionable):
- Score features on (Customer pain x # customers affected x Engineering risk) => prioritize high pain, many customers, low risk.
- Apply an urgency multiplier when feature prevents regulatory or contract breaches.

Mapping to stakeholders (who to loop):
- PMs: product-hosted-api (fallbacks, batching), product-console (rollouts), product-optimize (cost), product-private (onboarding).
- Eng: serving-runtime (batching runtime changes), console-and-tooling (visibility), developer-experience (SDK fixes).
- Compliance/security: review for eval-rollouts and any prompt storage.
- CS/AE: communicate quick-win schedule and own the customer comms.

Immediate next steps (1–2 week plan):
1) Triage meeting (CS x PM x Eng leads) — target July 19. Agenda: accept/reject proposed quick-wins A–C and assign owners.
2) Draft PRD stub for A (fallback visibility) with API spec + console checkbox copy — due July 24.
3) Publish private onboarding checklist doc in Console help center and attach to onboarding playbook — owner: Mariana Lopez, due July 25.
4) Start scoping sessions for B (batching override) with runtime team — rough estimates by July 31.

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- Pull sample logs for last 3 customer incidents where fallback occurred (JIRA-INC-…); include in PRD appendix.
- Coordinate with billing team about feasibility of token-level compute costing (tagging floor).
- Keep a rolling list of customers who asked for each micro-theme (for outreach if feature ships).

Appendix: quick counts (from intake sources) — simple heuristics, not exhaustive:
- Fallback visibility mentions: ~18 distinct customers (12 enterprise, 6 mid-market).
- Batching frustration mentions: ~22 customers (mostly real-time/low-latency use cases).
- Rollout/eval requests: ~14 customers actively calling this out.

End of note — use this doc as the working artifact; please add inline comments and ping on #cs-field for triage meeting coordination.
